question: Can an energy that is nonconvex under linear mixing of densities become convex along mass-transport interpolations, thereby proving existence and uniqueness of equilibrium for attracting gases?

key_findings.claim: The paper introduces displacement interpolation by pushing one density along straight trajectories to the gradient-of-convex-potential map that transports it to a second density.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 1.1 sets rho_t = ((1-t)id + t grad psi)#rho. Propositions 1.3-1.5 establish absolute continuity, reversal and subdivision consistency, covariance under Euclidean symmetries and dilation, and the exceptional role of translations.

key_findings.claim: A broad class of internal energies is convex along displacement paths under what became known as McCann's condition.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 2.2 proves displacement convexity of integral A(rho) when lambda^d A(lambda^-d) is convex and nonincreasing. The proof converts local volume deformation under the monotone map into a matrix-determinant inequality and a change-of-variables formula.

key_findings.claim: The same geometry yields sharp norm concavity inequalities that include Brunn-Minkowski as a special case.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 2.3 gives a displacement concavity relation for a power of the Lq norm across the relevant q range; applying it to normalized indicators of compact sets recovers concavity of volume^(1/d) under Minkowski addition.

key_findings.claim: For a coercive convex attractive interaction and an admissible pressure law, the gas energy has a minimizer that is unique up to translation under strict attraction.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.1 uses tightness modulo translations and lower semicontinuity for existence. Convexity of both internal and pair-interaction energy along displacement paths gives uniqueness; equality analysis shows distinct minimizers can only translate one another under the stated strictness conditions.

key_findings.claim: The contribution is a foundational geometric principle, but it does not cover arbitrary gas attractions or prove dynamical convergence to equilibrium.
key_findings.evidence: The main gas theorem assumes absolutely continuous probability densities on Euclidean space, a convex/coercive pair potential and a pressure growth condition. Nonconvex short-range/long-range interactions, singular measures, boundary effects, rates, and time-dependent gas equations are outside the paper.

method.core_idea: Replace linear interpolation of densities by optimal-transport displacement paths, along which compression and pair-interaction energies recover convexity.
method.mechanism: A Brenier monotone map pairs mass elements, straight-line motion defines intermediate measures, determinant inequalities control density compression, and convexity of the interaction potential controls pairwise separation. Direct-method compactness then produces a minimizer and strict displacement convexity produces uniqueness modulo translations.
assumptions: Endpoint measures are absolutely continuous probabilities on R^d.
The internal energy density satisfies the displacement-convexity scaling condition derived from the pressure law.
The even pair potential is convex, coercive, and sufficiently strict for uniqueness.
Energy is translation invariant, so uniqueness can only be stated modulo translations.

techniques.role: Defines a nonlinear convexity geometry on probability densities through optimal mass transport.
Represents the mass correspondence as the gradient of a convex potential.
Turns local Jacobian evolution into convexity of integral density energies.
Prevents escaping mass and establishes an equilibrium minimizer despite symmetry.

evaluations.setting: Abstract internal energies and absolutely continuous probability densities on Euclidean space
evaluations.metric: convexity along the proposed interpolation and sharp functional inequalities
evaluations.result: Proves internal-energy displacement convexity, Lq power inequalities, and a measure-level Brunn-Minkowski generalization.
evaluations.baseline: Ordinary linear mixing, for which the complete gas energy need not be convex.

evaluations.setting: Attracting gas with pressure-derived internal energy and convex pair potential
evaluations.metric: existence and uniqueness of energy minimizers
evaluations.result: Establishes a ground state and uniqueness up to translation under strict attraction, with a radial-potential relaxation.
evaluations.baseline: Prior convexity and rearrangement arguments requiring different symmetry or functional assumptions.

limitations: The equilibrium theorem addresses a deliberately restricted convex-attraction gas model rather than realistic nonconvex or singular interactions.
Absolute continuity and Euclidean geometry exclude atoms, manifolds, discrete spaces, and constrained domains in the stated framework.
No numerical algorithm, gradient-flow construction, convergence rate, or physical-data comparison is provided.
Strict convexity can fail along translations and other equality cases, so uniqueness needs careful qualification.
Some transport change-of-variables arguments require the substantial technical regularity developed in Section 4.
failure_modes: A nonconvex interaction energy destroys displacement convexity and permits multiple equilibria or pattern formation.
Insufficient coercivity allows a minimizing sequence to spread or split mass at infinity.
A pressure law outside McCann's scaling range makes internal energy concave along some transport paths.
Singular densities invalidate the paper's pointwise Jacobian proof without relaxation to a broader measure space.
reusable_insights: Choose an interpolation adapted to the state geometry before concluding that an energy is nonconvex.
For probability models, geodesic convexity can yield uniqueness and stability unavailable under mixture convexity.
Always audit equality cases induced by symmetries before claiming a unique optimizer.
Scaling a density under dilation is a fast diagnostic for plausible displacement-convex internal energies.
open_questions: Which nonconvex or singular interaction energies retain weaker uniqueness or convergence properties?
How do displacement-convex energies behave on manifolds, bounded domains, graphs, and nonlinear-mobility geometries?
What computational schemes best exploit displacement convexity at high dimension?
Can approximate displacement convexity provide quantitative metastability guarantees when exact convexity fails?

competitive_landscape.title: Eulerian calculus for the displacement convexity in the Wasserstein distance
competitive_landscape.difference: Daneri and Savare give an Eulerian proof on compact Riemannian manifolds with Ricci lower bounds, avoiding the global-map regularity route central to McCann's Euclidean proof.

competitive_landscape.title: Nonlinear mobility continuity equations and generalized displacement convexity
competitive_landscape.difference: Carrillo et al. replace linear mobility by a concave nonlinear mobility and generalize McCann's internal-energy condition, while showing potential and interaction energies may lose semiconvexity in the new geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Nonconvex gradient flow in the Wasserstein metric and applications to constrained nonlocal interactions
competitive_landscape.difference: Craig develops well-posedness and discrete-flow convergence beyond semiconvex energies for constrained nonlocal interactions. It addresses precisely the important regimes where McCann's convexity certificate is unavailable.

competitive_landscape.title: Guaranteeing Higher Order Convergence Rates for Accelerated Wasserstein Gradient Flow Schemes
competitive_landscape.difference: Chu and Jacobs use lambda-displacement convexity to prove stability and convergence of higher-order minimizing-movement schemes, illustrating how the reviewed structural property now powers algorithms rather than only equilibrium proofs.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after historical and current primary-source comparison: this is a seminal paper that introduces displacement convexity as a usable principle, proves the foundational internal-energy condition and functional inequalities, and applies them to an equilibrium uniqueness problem. Later Wasserstein gradient-flow theory and generalized geometries extend rather than displace the central idea; the principal qualification is its restrictive convex-attraction/static setting.
reviewer_notes: Reviewed all 27 journal pages, including interpolation properties, internal-energy and norm theorems, Brunn-Minkowski corollary, gas minimizer proof, equality cases, lower-semicontinuity lemmas, and the full change-of-variables appendix. Seven primary publisher/arXiv sources spanning predecessor, direct descendants, nonconvex alternatives, and current algorithms were checked on 2026-08-23.
